Physics.chapter: Dual nature of radiation and matter

disputedQuestionsDossier.subject: Physics
disputedQuestionsDossier.acceptedKey: Option D (Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect)
disputedQuestionsDossier.summary: Statement II claimed 'Atoms of each element are stable and emit their characteristic spectrum.' Old NCERT Physics said 'atoms of each element are stable', while New Rationalized NCERT changed it to 'atoms of most elements are stable'. NTA initially gave +4 grace/alternative marks to Option A ('Both correct'), inflating 720/720 toppers from 17 to 67 (44 from this single question). On July 23, 2024, the Supreme Court accepted a 3-member IIT Delhi panel report ruling ONLY Option D is scientifically & NCERT-compliant, revoking the bonus for 4.2+ lakh candidates.

disputedQuestionsDossier.subject: Chemistry
disputedQuestionsDossier.acceptedKey: Option A or Option B ([Co(NH3)3Cl3] or [Co(NH3)4Cl2])
disputedQuestionsDossier.summary: Asked which complex has minimum molar conductance in solution. While [Co(NH3)3Cl3] is a neutral non-electrolyte (0 ions), Option 2 was printed in the booklet as [Co(NH3)4Cl2] without the outer chloride counter-ion (making it appear neutral as well). NTA's Final Answer Key officially awarded +4 marks to candidates who marked EITHER Option 1 (A) OR Option 2 (B).

disputedQuestionsDossier.subject: Zoology
disputedQuestionsDossier.status: Supreme Court Challenge Dismissed (Single Key Retained)
disputedQuestionsDossier.acceptedKey: Option B (a, c and e only — 3 correct statements)
disputedQuestionsDossier.summary: Multi-statement question (a–e) on Cardiac Cycle events (SAN 70–75/min, AVN action potential, ventricular systole, joint diastole). Petitioners in Shivam Gandhi & Ors. vs NTA (July 2025) argued NCERT line ambiguity on statement (d)/(b). The Supreme Court refused to interfere with NTA's subject-expert key (Option B).

disputedQuestionsDossier.qNum: Biology Q.153 (Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants)
disputedQuestionsDossier.subject: Botany
disputedQuestionsDossier.acceptedKey: Option A (Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A)
disputedQuestionsDossier.summary: Assertion (A): 'A typical unfertilised, angiosperm embryo sac at maturity is 8 nucleate and 7-celled.' Reason (R): 'The egg apparatus has 2 polar nuclei.' Wait — in Code 45 Q153 (Tapetum nourishment / microspore mother cell), coaching institutes debated whether R directly explains A, or in the Fig-Wasp question (Q157) whether wasp lays eggs in all fig species. NTA retained its strict NCERT key.

disputedQuestionsDossier.subject: Physics
disputedQuestionsDossier.summary: Vernier Calliper question with N divisions on main scale coinciding with (N+1) divisions on Vernier scale and a negative zero error of 2 divisions. None of the 4 printed algebraic options matched the dimensionally valid corrected reading formula, forcing NTA to drop Q.26 and award +4 bonus marks to all candidates.

disputedQuestionsDossier.subject: Zoology
disputedQuestionsDossier.summary: Multi-statement question (A–E) on Henle's Loop, Vasa Recta, and PCT osmolarity where two statements were simultaneously false/contradictory against the printed option combinations. Officially dropped in Final Answer Key (+4 to all).

disputedQuestionsDossier.subject: Zoology
disputedQuestionsDossier.summary: Chronological ordering of vertebrate evolution stages (Jawless fish -> Lobefins -> Amphibians -> Reptiles) had an ambiguous directional phrasing in the stem; NTA's Final Answer Key accepted both Option A and Option C for +4 marks.

examShocksTimeline.headline: COVID Protocol & Introduction of 200-Question Section-B Pattern
examShocksTimeline.impact: NTA introduced Section A (35 Qs compulsory) + Section B (15 Qs, attempt any 10) per subject and extended duration to 200 minutes. Directly caused top-score inflation (Soyeb Aftab & Akanksha Singh first-ever 720/720 in 2020; 3 toppers at 720/720 in 2021).

examShocksTimeline.headline: Surge of Statement I/II, Assertion-Reason & Match-List Traps
examShocksTimeline.impact: While Physics numericals stayed formula-based, NTA transformed Biology into a high-density reading test: Statement I/II, Assertion-Reason, and 5-statement (a,b,c,d,e) questions jumped from <3% (2018) to >24% (2022–2023). Tamil Nadu's Prabanjan J scored 720/720 (AIR 1) in NEET 2023.

examShocksTimeline.headline: NMC Syllabus Rationalization, 67 Toppers Crisis, Grace Marks & Supreme Court Re-NEET
examShocksTimeline.impact: NMC pruned 18 chapters across PCB but added Experimental Skills & new Plant Families. Time-loss grace marks (1,563 students) + the Physics 'Atoms' old-vs-new NCERT key caused 67 candidates to hit 720/720. The Supreme Court ordered Re-NEET for 1,563 grace-mark candidates (June 23, 2024) and appointed an IIT-Delhi panel that revoked the Physics Atoms bonus, dropping 720/720 toppers to 17 and lowering cutoffs by ~1–2 marks.

examShocksTimeline.headline: Section-B Abolished (180 Qs in 180 Mins) & Toughest Physics Paper Since 2016
examShocksTimeline.impact: On Jan 25, 2025, NTA abolished Section B and the extra 20 minutes, reverting to 180 compulsory questions in 180 minutes. The May 4, 2025 paper featured lengthy multi-concept Physics numericals and dense multi-statement Biology. Zero students scored 720/720 (AIR 1 Mahesh Kumar scored 686/720), and Tamil Nadu Govt MBBS General (OC) Round 1 cutoff dropped by ~119 marks (from 660 in 2024 to 541 in 2025).

examShocksTimeline.headline: NEET 2026 (Code 11) & Re-NEET 2026 (Code 50) — Strict NCERT + Experimental Skills Era
examShocksTimeline.impact: Continued the strict 180-question, 180-minute compulsory format with heavy emphasis on Experimental Physics (Vernier Calliper, Screw Gauge, Meter Bridge), Coordination/Organic qualitative analysis, and multi-statement NCERT Biology.

patternShifts.summary: Foundational NCERT + classic CBSE conceptual numericals in Mechanics, Electrodynamics, Equilibrium, Coordination Chemistry, Genetics, and Human Physiology — frequently recycled verbatim into modern NEET Statement questions.
84%–89% single-line direct NCERT fact & formula MCQs; near-zero Statement I/II or Assertion-Reason traps.

Optional Section B cushioned tough numericals, driving massive top-score bunching in 2024 (67 candidates at 720/720 before SC IIT-Delhi Atoms revision to 17) while NTA surged Match-List, Statement I/II, and Assertion-Reason questions to ~25% of the paper.

NTA removed Section B and the extra 20 minutes. NEET 2025 shocked aspirants (AIR 1 Mahesh Kumar at 686/720) with multi-concept Physics numericals and dense multi-statement Biology under a strict 1-minute-per-question clock.

controversiesAndLessons.title: NEET 2024 Physics 'Atoms' Controversy (Supreme Court & IIT Delhi Verdict)
controversiesAndLessons.detail: Statement I ('Atoms are electrically neutral...') vs Statement II ('Atoms of each element are stable and emit their characteristic spectrum'). Over 4.2 lakh students marked 'Both True' based on older pre-rationalized NCERT printings. The Supreme Court appointed a 3-professor IIT Delhi panel, which ruled ONLY 'Statement I correct, Statement II incorrect' is valid (radioactive elements are unstable) — proving NEW rationalized NCERT editions strictly govern NTA keys.

controversiesAndLessons.title: NEET 2025 Chemistry Q63 Minimum Conductance (Dual Key A & B) & Biology SC Challenge
controversiesAndLessons.detail: In NEET 2025 (Code 45), Chemistry Q63 on minimum molar conductance between [Co(NH3)3Cl3] and [Co(NH3)4Cl2] had TWO official keys accepted (Options 1 & 2) in NTA's Final Answer Key. Meanwhile, Biology Q112 (Cardiac cycle events), Q153 (Tapetum), and Q157 (Fig-Wasp) were challenged up to the Supreme Court (Shivam Gandhi vs NTA, July 2025), which declined to override NTA's expert committee.

controversiesAndLessons.title: Re-NEET 2026 Dropped Bonus (+4 to All) & Multi-Key Rulings
controversiesAndLessons.detail: In Re-NEET 2026 (Code 50), NTA officially dropped Physics Q26 (Vernier Calliper negative zero error formula defect) and Biology Q157 (Henle's Loop / Vasa Recta counter-current), awarding +4 bonus marks to all candidates, and accepted both Options A & C for Biology Q159 (Evolution chronology).

controversiesAndLessons.title: Old vs. New NMC Rationalized Syllabus Boundary
controversiesAndLessons.detail: Topics like p-Block compounds, States of Matter, s-Block, Transport in Plants, Mineral Nutrition, and Digestion were pruned in NMC rationalization, yet experimental skills (Vernier calliper, Screw gauge, Salt analysis, Lassaigne/Kjeldahl organic tests) and Plant Families (Malvaceae, Cruciferae, Compositae, Gramineae) saw sharp weightage spikes.

coachingAndRedditMeta.source: Aakash CST (Complete Syllabus Tests) & Intensive Batch
coachingAndRedditMeta.verdict: Ranked #1 on r/MEDICOreTARDS & r/JEENEETards for Biology NCERT line-twisting and exact NTA statement/Assertion-Reason phrasing.
Deliberately 15–20% tougher in Physics & Physical Chemistry than typical NEET — gold standard for surviving a 2025-style tough Physics paper without panicking.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Physics — Physics NCERT Core (Code 11, Q.1)
questions.stem_en: The speed of light in vacuum is taken as unity. If light takes $6\text{ min } 40\text{ s}$ to reach the Earth from the Sun, the distance between the Sun and the Earth in new unit is:
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Physics: Physics NCERT Core] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
**Sol.** Time, $t = 6\text{ min } 40\text{ s}$
$= 360 + 40$
$= 400\text{ s}$

Distance in new system $d = vt$
$= 1 \times 400 = 400$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் D** ($400$). பாடம்: Physics NCERT Core.
questions.ncert_key_point: [NEET 2026 Official • Numerical / Formula] Official Key: Option D — Physics NCERT Core (Class 12).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Physics — System of Particles and Rotational Motion (Code 11, Q.4)
questions.stem_en: The angular speed of a flywheel is increased from $600\text{ rpm}$ to $1200\text{ rpm}$ in $10\text{ s}$. The number of revolutions completed by the flywheel during this time is:
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Physics: System of Particles and Rotational Motion] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. $\alpha = \frac{\omega_2 - \omega_1}{\Delta t} = \left(\frac{1200 - 600}{10}\right)\frac{2\pi}{60} = 2\pi\text{ rad/s}^2$

$\Rightarrow$ Use equation of motion, $\omega_2^2 = \omega_1^2 + 2\alpha\theta$

$\Rightarrow \omega_2 = 1200 \times \frac{2\pi}{60} = 40\pi$

$\omega_1 = 600 \times \frac{2\pi}{60} = 20\pi$

$(40\pi)^2 = (20\pi)^2 + 2 \times 2\pi\theta$

$\Rightarrow 1200 \pi^2 = 4\pi\theta$

$\Rightarrow \theta = 300\pi\text{ radian}$

$\Rightarrow \text{Number of revolution} = \frac{\theta}{2\pi} = 150$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் C** (150). பாடம்: System of Particles and Rotational Motion.
questions.ncert_key_point: [NEET 2026 Official • Direct NCERT Concept] Official Key: Option C — System of Particles and Rotational Motion (Class 11).

questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Physics — Current Electricity (Code 11, Q.6)
questions.stem_en: A resistor is connected to a battery of $12\text{ V}$ emf and internal resistance $2\ \Omega$. If the current in the circuit is $0.6\text{ A}$, the terminal voltage of the battery is:
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Physics: Current Electricity] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. Circuit can be draw as,

$\Rightarrow$ Terminal voltage of battery $V = E - ir$
$= 12 - 0.6 \times 2 = 10.8\text{ V}$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் D** (10.8 V). பாடம்: Current Electricity.
questions.ncert_key_point: [NEET 2026 Official • Numerical / Formula] Official Key: Option D — Current Electricity (Class 12).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Physics — Physics NCERT Core (Code 11, Q.7)
questions.stem_en:
A flask contains argon and chlorine in the ratio of $2 : 1$ by mass. The temperature of the mixture is $27^\circ\text{C}$. The ratio of root mean square speed of the molecules of the two gases $\left(\frac{V_{\text{rms}}^{\text{Ar}}}{V_{\text{rms}}^{\text{Cl}}}\right)$ is:

(Atomic mass of argon $= 40.0\text{ u}$ and molecular mass of chlorine $= 70.0\text{ u}$)
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Physics: Physics NCERT Core] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. $V_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}}$

For same temperature, $V_{\text{rms}} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{M}}$

$$\frac{V_{\text{rms}}^{\text{Ar}}}{V_{\text{rms}}^{\text{Cl}}} = \sqrt{\frac{M_{\text{Cl}}}{M_{\text{Ar}}}} = \sqrt{\frac{70}{40}} = \frac{\sqrt{7}}{2}$$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் A** ($\frac{\sqrt{7}}{2}$). பாடம்: Physics NCERT Core.
questions.ncert_key_point: [NEET 2026 Official • Numerical / Formula] Official Key: Option A — Physics NCERT Core (Class 12).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Physics — Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter (Code 11, Q.9)
questions.stem_en:
Match List I with List II.

| | List-I | | List-II |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| A. | $E = h\nu$ | I. | de Broglie wavelength |
| B. | Diffraction and Interference | II. | Particle nature of light |
| C. | $\lambda = h/p$ | III. | Wave nature of light |
| D. | Compton effect | IV. | Energy of photon |

Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Physics: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
**Sol.**

A. $E = h\nu$ is energy of photon

B. Diffraction and interference confirm wave nature of light

C. $\lambda = \frac{h}{p}$ is de Broglie wavelength of particle.

D. Compton effect confirms particle nature of light.
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் D** (A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II). பாடம்: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter.
questions.ncert_key_point: [NEET 2026 Official • Match List-I & II] Official Key: Option D — Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter (Class 12).

**Sol.**

questions.subject: Physics
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Physics — Work, Energy and Power (Code 11, Q.13)
questions.stem_en: The amount of work done to raise a mass '$m$' from the surface of the Earth to a height equal to the radius of the Earth '$R$' will be
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Physics: Work, Energy and Power] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
Answer (4)
Sol. W.D. = $U_2 - U_1$

$= -\frac{GMm}{R+R} - \left(-\frac{GMm}{R}\right)$

$= -\frac{GMm}{2R} + \frac{GMm}{R}$

$= \frac{GMm}{2R} = \frac{mgR}{2}$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் D** ($mg\frac{R}{2}$). பாடம்: Work, Energy and Power.
questions.ncert_key_point: [NEET 2026 Official • Direct NCERT Concept] Official Key: Option D — Work, Energy and Power (Class 11).

questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Physics — Units and Measurements (Code 11, Q.14)
questions.stem_en: Each side of a metallic cube of mass $5.580\text{ kg}$ is measured to the $9.0\text{ cm}$. Keeping the significant figures in view, the density of the material of the cube can be best expressed as $X \times 10^3\text{ kg m}^{-3}$ where the value of $X$ is:
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Physics: Units and Measurements] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
$\text{Sol. Density} = = \frac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Volume}}$

$= \frac{5.580\text{ kg}}{(9.0\text{ cm})^3}$

$= \frac{5.580}{729} \times 10^6 \frac{\text{kg}}{\text{m}^3}$

$= 0.007654321 \times 10^6 \frac{\text{kg}}{\text{m}^3}$

$= 7.654 \times 10^3 \frac{\text{kg}}{\text{m}^3}$

$= 7.7 \times 10^3 \frac{\text{kg}}{\text{m}^3}$

Hence, on comparing

$X = 7.7$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் D** (7.7). பாடம்: Units and Measurements.

questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Physics — Work, Energy and Power (Code 11, Q.16)
questions.stem_en:
The sum of kinetic energy and potential energy of a simple pendulum bob is $0.02\text{ joule}$. The speed of the simple pendulum bob at equilibrium position is approximately:
(Consider mass of the bob = $20\text{ g}$)
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Physics: Work, Energy and Power] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
At equilibrium position

Total energy = K.E

$\frac{1}{2}mv^2 = 0.02$

$\frac{1}{2} \times 20 \times v^2 \times 10^{-3} = 2 \times 10^{-2}$

$v = \sqrt{2}$

$v = 1.41\text{ m/s}$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் B** (1.41 m/s). பாடம்: Work, Energy and Power.

questions.stem_en: In Young's double slit experiment, using monochromatic light of wavelength $\lambda$, the intensity of light at a point on the screen where the path difference is $\lambda$, is $K$ units. The intensity of light at a point where the path difference is $\frac{\lambda}{3}$ will be
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Physics: Wave Optics] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)

Sol. $I = I_0 \cos^2 \frac{\Delta\phi}{2}$ [$I_0 \rightarrow$ maximum intensity]

$I = I_0 \cos^2 \frac{K\Delta x}{2}$

$K = I_0 \cos^2 \left(\frac{2\pi}{\lambda} \times \frac{\lambda}{2}\right)$

$K = I_0$

$K_1 = I_0 \cos^2 \left(\frac{2\pi}{\lambda} \times \frac{\lambda}{3 \times 2}\right) = I_0 \cos^2 \left(\frac{\pi}{3}
ight)$

$K_1 = \frac{I_0}{4}$

$\frac{K}{K_1} = 4 \Rightarrow K_1 = \frac{K}{4}$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் A** ($\frac{K}{4}$). பாடம்: Wave Optics.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Physics — Wave Optics (Code 11, Q.20)
questions.stem_en:
In interference and diffraction, the light energy is redistributed. If it reduces in one region, producing a dark fringe, it increases in another region, producing a bright fringe.

A. As there is no gain or loss of energy, these phenomena are consistent with the principle of conservation of energy.

B. Diffraction and interference are characteristics exhibited only by light waves.

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Physics: Wave Optics] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)

choices.text_en: A is true and B is also true
choices.text_ta: A is true and B is also true

choices.text_en: A is false, but B is true
choices.text_ta: A is false, but B is true

choices.text_en: A is true, but B is false
choices.text_ta: A is true, but B is false

choices.text_en: Both A and B are false
choices.text_ta: Both A and B are false

questions.explanation_en:
Sol. In interference and diffraction there is no loss of energy, the energy gets redistributed.
Interference and diffraction both are exhibited in light as well as sound waves.
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் C** (A is true, but B is false). பாடம்: Wave Optics.
questions.ncert_key_point: [NEET 2026 Official • Direct NCERT Concept] Official Key: Option C — Wave Optics (Class 12).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Physics — Physics NCERT Core (Code 11, Q.21)
questions.stem_en:
For a travelling harmonic wave
$y(x, t) = 2.0 \cos 2\pi(10t - 0.0080x + 0.35)$, where $x$ and $y$ are in $\text{cm}$ and $t$ in $\text{s}$. The phase difference between oscillatory motion of two points separated by a distance of $0.5\text{ m}$ is:
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Physics: Physics NCERT Core] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. $y(x, t) = 2.0 \cos 2\pi(10t - 0.008x + 0.35)$

Total phase

$\phi = 20\pi - 2\pi \times 8 \times 10^{-3}x + 2\pi \times 0.35$

$\Delta\phi = k\Delta x$

$\Delta\phi = 2\pi \times 8 \times 10^{-3}\ \Delta x$

$= 2\pi \times 8 \times 10^{-3} \times \left(\frac{100}{2}\right)$

$= 8\pi \times 10^{-1} = 0.8\pi$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் B** ($0.8\ \pi\text{ rad}$). பாடம்: Physics NCERT Core.
questions.ncert_key_point: [NEET 2026 Official • Direct NCERT Concept] Official Key: Option B — Physics NCERT Core (Class 12).

questions.stem_en: The magnitude and direction of the acceleration produced in a body of mass $5\text{ kg}$ when two mutually perpendicular forces $8\text{ N}$ and $6\text{ N}$ act on it, are respectively:

questions.explanation_en:
Sol. 

$F_{\text{net}} = \sqrt{6^2 + 8^2}$

$a = \frac{F_{\text{net}}}{m} = \frac{10}{5} = 2\text{ m/s}^2$

$\tan\theta = \frac{6}{8}$

$\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)$ from $8\text{ N}$

questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Physics — Electrostatic Potential and Capacitance (Code 11, Q.23)
questions.stem_en: Consider two uncharged capacitors of equal capacitance $200\text{ pF}$. One of them is charged by a $100\text{ V}$ supply and disconnected. Now this capacitor is connected to the uncharged capacitor. The amount of electrostatic energy lost in the process is:
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Physics: Electrostatic Potential and Capacitance] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
$\text{Sol. Energy loss} = \frac{1}{2} \frac{C_1C_2}{C_1 + C_2} V^2$
$= \frac{1}{2} \left( \frac{200 \times 200}{400} \right) \times 10^{-12}(100)^2$
$= \frac{1}{2} \times 10^6 \times 10^{-12} = 0.5 \times 10^{-6}\text{ J}$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் A** ($0.5 \times 10^{-6}\text{ J}$). பாடம்: Electrostatic Potential and Capacitance.

questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Physics — Physics NCERT Core (Code 11, Q.24)
questions.stem_en: The power of a crane, which lifts a mass of $1000\text{ kg}$ to a height of $20\text{ m}$ in $10\text{ s}$ is: ($g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Physics: Physics NCERT Core] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)

$\text{Sol. Power} = \frac{\text{Work}}{\text{Time}}$
$= \frac{mgh}{t}$
$= \frac{10^3 \times 9.8 \times 20}{10} = 19.6\text{ kW}$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் C** ($19.6\text{ kW}$). பாடம்: Physics NCERT Core.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Physics — Units and Measurements (Code 11, Q.25)
questions.stem_en: In a vernier calliper, $20\text{ VSD}$ coincide with $16\text{ MSD}$ (each division of length $1\text{ mm}$). The least count of the vernier callipers is:
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Physics: Units and Measurements] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
$\text{Sol. Least count of vernier callipers}$
$\text{L.C.} = 1\text{ MSD} - 1\text{ VSD} \quad \dots\text{(i)}$
$20\text{ VSD} = 16\text{ MSD}$
$1\text{ VSD} = \frac{16}{20}\text{ MSD}$
$\text{From (i)}$
$\text{L.C.} = 1\text{ MSD} - \frac{16}{20}\text{ MSD}$
$\text{L.C.} = \frac{4}{20}\text{ MSD}$
$\text{L.C.} = \frac{1}{5}\text{ mm} = 0.2\text{ mm}$
$\text{L.C.} = 0.02\text{ cm}$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் C** ($0.02\text{ cm}$). பாடம்: Units and Measurements.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Physics — Physics NCERT Core (Code 11, Q.26)
questions.stem_en:
When a ruler falls vertically, 5 different persons catch it with different reaction times. ($g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}$)

A. Person A has reaction time of 0.20 s.
B. Person B has reaction time of 0.22 s.
C. Person C has reaction time of 0.18 s.
D. Person D has reaction time of 0.19 s.
E. Person E has reaction time of 0.21 s.

What is the **correct** order of the distance travelled by the ruler for each person?
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Physics: Physics NCERT Core] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. $\rightarrow$ There will be large distance for large reaction time

$\rightarrow$ Descending order of reaction time

$\Rightarrow t_B > t_E > t_A > t_D > t_C$

$\rightarrow$ Descending order of distance covered

$\Rightarrow S_B > S_E > S_A > S_D > S_C$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் C** (B > E > A > D > C). பாடம்: Physics NCERT Core.
questions.ncert_key_point: [NEET 2026 Official • Direct NCERT Concept] Official Key: Option C — Physics NCERT Core (Class 12).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Physics — Physics NCERT Core (Code 11, Q.28)
questions.stem_en: A room heater is rated 400 W, 220 V. If the supply voltage drops to 200 V, what will be the power consumed (approximately)?
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Physics: Physics NCERT Core] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
**Sol.** Rated power of heater

$P_0 = \frac{V_0^2}{R}$ ...(i)

Consumed power

$P_c = \frac{V^2}{R}$ ...(ii) [$V \rightarrow$ applied voltage]

From (i) and (ii)

$\frac{P_c}{P_0} = \frac{V^2}{V_0^2}$

$P_c = \left[ \frac{V}{V_0} \right]^2 P_0$

$P_c = \left[ \frac{200}{220} \right]^2 \times 400$

$P_c = 331 \text{ W}$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் C** (331 W). பாடம்: Physics NCERT Core.
questions.ncert_key_point: [NEET 2026 Official • Numerical / Formula] Official Key: Option C — Physics NCERT Core (Class 12).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Physics — Moving Charges and Magnetism (Code 11, Q.29)
questions.stem_en:
A 100-turn closely wound circular coil of radius 5 cm has a magnetic field of $3.14 \times 10^{-3}$ T at its centre. The current flowing through the coil, and the magnitude of the magnetic moment of this coil are, respectively :

(Take $\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}$ T m/A)
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Physics: Moving Charges and Magnetism] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
**Sol.** Magnetic field of a circular loop:

$B_0 = \frac{\mu_0 Ni}{2R}$

$$i = \frac{2RB_0}{\mu_0 N} = \frac{2 \times 5 \times 10^{-2} \times 3.14 \times 10^{-3}}{4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 100}$$

$i = 2.5 \text{ A}$

Magnetic moment

$M = NiA$

$= 100 \times 2.5 \times 3.14 \times (5 \times 10^{-2})^2\ [\because A = \pi R^2]$

$= 2 \text{ A m}^2$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் D** (2.5 A, 2 A m$^2$). பாடம்: Moving Charges and Magnetism.
questions.ncert_key_point: [NEET 2026 Official • Numerical / Formula] Official Key: Option D — Moving Charges and Magnetism (Class 12).

questions.stem_en: A rectangular wire loop of sides $8\text{ cm}$ and $3\text{ cm}$ with a small cut, is moving out of a region of uniform magnetic field of magnitude $0.3\text{ T}$ directed normal to the plane of the loop. The emf developed across the cut, if the velocity of the loop is $2\text{ cm s}^{-1}$, in a direction normal to the shorter side of the loop, will be :
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Physics: Electromagnetic Induction] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
Induced emf across the shorter side

$E_{\text{induced}} = Bvl \quad [\because \vec{B} \perp \vec{V} \perp \vec{l}]$

$= 0.3 \times 2 \times 10^{-2} \times 3 \times 10^{-2}$

$= 1.8 \times 10^{-4}\text{ V}$

$= 1.8 \times 10^{-4}\text{ volt}$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் D** ($1.8 \times 10^{-4}\text{ volt}$). பாடம்: Electromagnetic Induction.

questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Physics — Nuclei (Code 11, Q.31)
questions.stem_en:
Four statements are given ($A$ is mass number):

A. The volume of a nucleus is proportional to $A^{1/3}$.

B. The volume of a nucleus is proportional to $A$.

C. The difference in mass of an atom and its nucleus is called the mass defect.

D. The difference in mass of a nucleus and its constituents is called the mass defect.

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Physics: Nuclei] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)

choices.text_en: A and C are true, but B and D are false
choices.text_ta: A and C are true, but B and D are false

choices.text_en: B and C are true, but A and D are false
choices.text_ta: B and C are true, but A and D are false

choices.text_en: A and D are true, but B and C are false
choices.text_ta: A and D are true, but B and C are false

choices.text_en: B and D are true, but A and C are false
choices.text_ta: B and D are true, but A and C are false

questions.explanation_en:
As we know,

Size of nucleus, $r = r_0(A)^{\frac{1}{3}}$

$\Rightarrow r^3 = r_0^3 \cdot A$

$\Rightarrow V \propto A \quad \left(\because V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\right)$

So, option A $\rightarrow$ wrong and B $\rightarrow$ correct

while the difference between the actual mass of nucleus and its constituents is called the mass defect.

$\therefore$ option C $\rightarrow$ wrong and D $\rightarrow$ correct
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் D** (B and D are true, but A and C are false). பாடம்: Nuclei.

questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Physics — Oscillations (Code 11, Q.33)
questions.stem_en: Savitha, a XI standard student, while conducting an experiment to determine the effective length of a simple pendulum $L$, notes down the data of time taken to complete 30 oscillations as $60\text{ s}$ and hence calculates the length of the simple pendulum as: (Take $\pi^2 = 9.8$, and $g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Physics: Oscillations] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
Time taken for 30 oscillations $= 60\text{ s}$

Time period of simple pendulum = Time taken for 1 oscillation

$\Rightarrow T = \frac{60}{30} = 2\text{ s}$

$$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{l}{g}} \Rightarrow l = \frac{gT^2}{4\pi^2} = \frac{9.8 \times 2 \times 2}{4 \times 9.8} = 1\text{ m}$$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Physics — Thermodynamics (Code 11, Q.34)
questions.stem_en: An electric heater supplies heat to a system at a rate of $100\text{ W}$. If the system performs work at a rate of $75\text{ J/s}$, then the rate at which internal energy increases will be:
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Physics: Thermodynamics] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
Using $1^{\text{st}}$ law of thermodynamics for electric heater,

$Q = \Delta U + W$

$\Rightarrow \frac{dQ}{dt} = \frac{d(\Delta U)}{dt} + \frac{dW}{dt}$

$\Rightarrow 100\text{ W} = \frac{d(\Delta U)}{dt} + 75\text{ W}$

$\therefore \frac{d(\Delta U)}{dt} = 25\text{ W}$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் D** (25 W). பாடம்: Thermodynamics.
questions.ncert_key_point: [NEET 2026 Official • Numerical / Formula] Official Key: Option D — Thermodynamics (Class 11).

questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Physics — Current Electricity (Code 11, Q.36)
questions.stem_en: A galvanometer of resistance $100\ \Omega$ gives full scale deflection for a current of $1\text{ mA}$. It is converted into an ammeter of range $0 - 10\text{ A}$. The shunt required is:
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Physics: Current Electricity] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
**Sol.** $i_G = 1\text{ mA} = 0.001\text{ A}$

$i_S = 10 - i_G \simeq 10\text{ A}$

Both shunt resistance and galvanometer are in parallel connection

$\therefore i_S r_S = i_G R_G$

$\Rightarrow 10 \times r_S = 0.001 \times 100$

$\Rightarrow r_S = 0.01\ \Omega$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் A** ($0.01\ \Omega$). பாடம்: Current Electricity.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Physics — Physics NCERT Core (Code 11, Q.38)
questions.stem_en: The peak value of an alternating current is $5\text{ A}$ and frequency is $60\text{ Hz}$. How long will the current, starting from zero, take to reach the peak value?
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Physics: Physics NCERT Core] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
**Answer (4)**

**Sol.** Alternating current,

$i = i_{\text{peak}} \sin(\omega t)$

where $\omega = 2\pi f = 2\pi \times 60 = 120\pi\text{ rad/s}$

$\Rightarrow i = 5\sin(120\pi t)$

$\Rightarrow 5 = 5\sin(120\pi t)$

$\Rightarrow \sin(120\pi t) = 1 = \sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$

$\therefore 120\pi t = \frac{\pi}{2}$

$\Rightarrow t = \frac{1}{240}\text{ s}$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் D** ($\frac{1}{240}\text{ s}$). பாடம்: Physics NCERT Core.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Physics — Electric Charges and Fields (Code 11, Q.41)
questions.stem_en:
Which of the following statements are correct?

A. Inside a conductor, the electrostatic field is zero.

B. Electric field at the surface of a charged conductor does not depend on its surface charge density.

C. The interior of a charged conductor can have no excess charge in the static situation.

D. At the surface of a charged conductor, the electrostatic field must be normal to the surface at every point.

E. The electrostatic potential is zero everywhere inside a charged conductor.

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Physics: Electric Charges and Fields] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
Answer (3)

**Sol.**

A. Electrostatic field is zero inside a conductor.

B. Electric field at the surface of a charged conductor $= \frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0} \hat{n}$, depends on surface charge density ($\sigma$).

C. The interior of a charged conductor cannot have any excess charge in the static situation.

D. At the surface of a charged conductor, the electrostatic field $\perp$ surface.

E. The electrostatic potential is constant and can be non-zero everywhere inside a charged conductor.
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் C** (A, C and D only). பாடம்: Electric Charges and Fields.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Physics — Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter (Code 11, Q.42)
questions.stem_en:
For a metal of work function 6.6 eV, which of the following wavelengths of incident radiation does ***not*** give rise to the photoelectric effect?
(Take Planck's constant as $6.6 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}$)
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Physics: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. For incident radiation having wavelength ($\lambda$), photoelectric effect doesn't occur when $\frac{hc}{\lambda} \frac{hc}{W_0}$

$\Rightarrow \lambda > \frac{6.6 \times 10^{-34} \times 3 \times 10^8}{6.6 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}}$

$\Rightarrow \lambda > \frac{3 \times 10^{-7}}{1.6}$

$\Rightarrow \lambda > \frac{300}{1.6}\text{nm}$

$\Rightarrow \lambda = 187.5\text{ nm}$

$\therefore$ Option (3) 200 nm is correct.

questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry — Chemical Thermodynamics (Code 11, Q.48)
questions.stem_en:
Consider the following reaction :

$\text{2A(g)} + \text{B(g)} \rightarrow \text{2D(g)}$

$$\Delta\text{U}^{\ominus} = -10\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\text{ and }\Delta\text{S}^{\ominus} = -44\text{ JK}^{-1}\text{ at 298 K.}$$

Identify the **correct** option with $\Delta\text{G}^{\ominus}$ for the reaction and spontaneity of the reaction at 298 K.

(Given : $\text{R} = 8.31\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}$)
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Chemistry: Chemical Thermodynamics] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. $\text{2A(g)} + \text{B(g)} \rightarrow \text{2D(g)}$

$\Delta\text{U}^\circ = -10\text{ kJ/mol}$

$\Delta\text{S}^\circ = -44\text{ J/K}$

$\Delta\text{H}^\circ = \Delta\text{U}^\circ + \Delta\text{n}_\text{g}\text{RT}$

$$\Delta\text{H}^\circ = -10 - \frac{1 \times 298 \times (8.31)}{1000} = -10 - 2.48 = -12.48\text{ kJ/mol}$$

$\Delta\text{G}^\circ = \Delta\text{H}^\circ - \text{T}\Delta\text{S}^\circ$

$= -12.48 - \frac{298 \times (-44)}{1000}$

$= -12.48 + 13.112$

$= +0.632\text{ kJ/mol}$

Since $\Delta\text{G}^\circ$ comes out to be positive, so given process is non-spontaneous.
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் C** ($+0.63568\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, non-spontaneous). பாடம்: Chemical Thermodynamics.
questions.ncert_key_point: [NEET 2026 Official • Numerical / Formula] Official Key: Option C — Chemical Thermodynamics (Class 11).

questions.stem_en:
In a qualitative analysis, $\text{Bi}^{3+}$ is detected by appearance of precipitate of $\text{BiO}(\text{OH})(\text{s})$. Calculate pH when the following equilibrium exists at $298\text{ K}$.
$$\text{BiO}(\text{OH})(\text{s}) \rightleftharpoons \text{BiO}^+(\text{aq}) + \text{OH}^-(\text{aq}), \text{ K} = 4 \times 10^{-10}$$
(Given : $\log2 = 0.3010$)
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Chemistry: Chemistry NCERT Core] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. $\text{BiO}(\text{OH})(\text{s}) \rightleftharpoons \underset{\text{s}}{\text{BiO}^+(\text{aq})} + \underset{\text{s}}{\text{OH}^-(\text{aq})}$

$\text{K} = \frac{[\text{BiO}^+][\text{OH}^-]}{[\text{BiO}(\text{OH})(\text{s})]}$

$\text{K} = \frac{[\text{BiO}^+][\text{OH}^-]}{1}$

$\text{K} = \text{s} \times \text{s} = \text{s}^2$

$\text{s} = \sqrt{\text{K}} = \sqrt{4 \times 10^{-10}} = 2 \times 10^{-5} \text{ M}$

$[\text{H}^+] = \frac{\text{K}_\text{w}}{[\text{OH}^-]} = \frac{1}{2} \times 10^{-9}, \text{ pH} = -\log[\text{H}^+] = 9 + \log 2 = 9.301$

questions.stem_en: A bulb is rated at 150 watt, converting 8% energy into light. If energy of one photon is $4.42 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J}$, how many photons are emitted by the bulb per second?
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Chemistry: Chemistry NCERT Core] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
**Sol.**

Energy = Power $\times$ time
$= 150\text{ watt} \times 1\text{ s}$
$= 150\text{ J}$

Energy converted to light $= \frac{150 \times 8}{100} = 12\text{ J}$

$E = nh\nu$

Energy of one photon $= 4.42 \times 10^{-19}$

So, $n = \text{number of photons} = \frac{E}{h\nu} = \frac{12}{4.42 \times 10^{-19}}$
$= 2.715 \times 10^{19}$

questions.stem_en: The correct order of increasing metallic character of $\text{Na}$, $\text{Be}$, $\text{P}$, $\text{Mg}$ and $\text{Si}$ is
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Chemistry: Structure of Atom] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
On moving left to right in a period, metallic character decreases and on moving top to bottom in a group, metallic character increases. So, the correct order of increasing metallic character is

$\text{P} < \text{Si} < \text{Be} < \text{Mg} < \text{Na}$

$\text{Electronegativity} \propto \frac{1}{\text{Metallic character}}$

$$\begin{array}{lccccc}
& \textbf{Na} & \textbf{Mg} & \textbf{Be} & \textbf{Si} & \textbf{P} \\
\textbf{Electronegativity (On Pauling scale)} & 0.9 & 1.2 & 1.5 & 1.8 & 2.1
\end{array}$$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் A** ($\text{P} < \text{Si} < \text{Be} < \text{Mg} < \text{Na}$). பாடம்: Structure of Atom.
questions.ncert_key_point: [NEET 2026 Official • Direct NCERT Concept] Official Key: Option A — Structure of Atom (Class 11).

Match List I with List II :

| | List I 
(Complex/ion) | | List II 
(Shape/geometry) |

| A. | $[\text{Pt}(\text{Cl}_2)(\text{NH}_3)_2]$ | (I) | Octahedral |
| B. | $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]\text{Cl}_3$ | (II) | Trigonal bipyramidal |
| C. | $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$ | (III) | Square planar |
| D. | $[\text{Fe}(\text{CO})_5]$ | (IV) | Tetrahedral |

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Chemistry: Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
* In $[\text{Pt}(\text{Cl}_2)(\text{NH}_3)_2]$; $\text{Pt}$ has $dsp^2$ hybridisation, so shape of complex is square planar.
* In $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]\text{Cl}_3$; $\text{Co}$ has $d^2sp^3$ hybridisation so shape of complex is octahedral.
* In $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$; $\text{Ni}$ has $sp^3$ hybridisation so shape of complex ion is tetrahedral.
* In $[\text{Fe}(\text{CO})_5]$; shape of complex is trigonal bipyramidal.

questions.stem_en:
Identify the correct statements :
(A) The molality of $2.5\text{ g}$ of ethanoic acid (Molar mass : $60\text{ g mol}^{-1}$) in $75\text{ g}$ of benzene solution is $0.556\text{ m}$.
(B) The molarity of a solution containing $5\text{ g}$ of $\text{NaOH}$ (molar mass : $40\text{ g mol}^{-1}$) in $450\text{ mL}$ of solution is $0.278\text{ M}$ at $298\text{ K}$.
(C) Aquatic species are more comfortable in cold water.
(D) The solubility of gas increases with decrease in pressure.
(E) For a binary mixture of $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$, the number of moles of $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ are $\text{n}_\text{A}$ and $\text{n}_\text{B}$ respectively. The mole fraction of $\text{B}$ will be $\text{x}_\text{B} = \frac{\text{n}_\text{A}}{\text{n}_\text{A} + \text{n}_\text{B}}$.

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
(1) A, B and C only
(2) A and B only
(3) A and C only
(4) A, D and E only
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Chemistry: Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
Sol.

(A) $\text{Molality} = \frac{2.5}{60} \times \frac{1000}{75} = 0.556\text{ molal}$

(B) $\text{Molarity} = \frac{5}{40} \times \frac{1000}{450} = 0.278\text{ M}$

(C) Aquatic species are more comfortable in cold water
$\text{Henry's Law } \text{K}_\text{H} \propto \text{Temp} \propto \frac{1}{\text{solubility}}$

(D) According to Henry's Law,
$\text{P} = \text{K}_\text{H}\text{x}$
$\text{P} \propto \text{x}$
$\text{P} \propto \text{Solubility}$
So as $\text{P}\uparrow$, solubility $\uparrow$

(E) $\text{x}_\text{B} = \frac{\text{n}_\text{B}}{\text{n}_\text{A} + \text{n}_\text{B}}$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் A** (A, B and C only). பாடம்: Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry.

questions.stem_en:
A solution of copper sulphate is electrolysed for 10 minutes with a current of 1.5 amperes. The mass of copper deposited at cathode is :

(Given : Molar mass of $\text{Cu} = 63\text{ g mol}^{-1}$; $1\text{ F} = 96487\text{ C mol}^{-1}$)
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Chemistry: Chemistry NCERT Core] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. $\text{CuSO}_4 \longrightarrow \text{Cu}^{2+} + \text{SO}_4^{2-}$

$2\text{e}^- + \text{Cu}^{2+} \longrightarrow \text{Cu(s)}$

$\text{W} = \text{zit}$

$= \frac{\text{E} \times \text{i} \times \text{t}}{96500}$

$= \frac{63 \times 1.5 \times 10 \times 60}{2 \times 96500}$

$= \frac{56,700}{193000} = 0.2938\text{ g}$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் B** (0.2938 g). பாடம்: Chemistry NCERT Core.

questions.stem_en: At a certain temperature, T (K), during a process, $500\text{ J}$ is absorbed by the system and work of $200\text{ J}$ is done by the system. Then change in internal energy of the system is :
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Chemistry: Chemical Thermodynamics] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. From first law of thermodynamics

$\Delta\text{U} = \text{q} + \text{w}$

$\text{q} = +500\text{ J}$

$\text{w} = -200\text{ J}$

$\Delta\text{U} = 500 - 200$

$= 300\text{ J}$

questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry — Equilibrium (Code 11, Q.78)
questions.stem_en:
At $298\text{ K}$, a certain buffer solution contains equal concentrations of $\text{X}^-$ and $\text{HX}$, $\text{K}_\text{b}$ for $\text{X}^-$ is $10^{-10}$.
What is the pH of this buffer solution?

(1) 2
(2) 4
(3) 6
(4) 10
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Chemistry: Equilibrium] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. $\text{HX} \rightleftharpoons \text{H}^+ + \text{X}^-$

$\text{K}_\text{a} \times \text{K}_\text{b} = \text{K}_\text{w}$

$\text{K}_\text{a} = \frac{\text{K}_\text{w}}{\text{K}_\text{b}} = \frac{10^{-14}}{10^{-10}} = 10^{-4}$

$\text{pH} = \text{pK}_\text{a} + \log\frac{[\text{X}^-]}{[\text{HX}]}$

Given that : $[\text{X}^-] = [\text{HX}]$

$= 4 + \log(1)$

$= 4 + 0$

$= 4$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் B** (4). பாடம்: Equilibrium.

questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry — Chemistry NCERT Core (Code 11, Q.79)
questions.stem_en:
Calculate emf of the half cell given below :
$\text{Pt (s)} \mid \text{H}_2\text{(g, 2 atm)} \mid \text{HCl (aq, 0.02 M)}$
$E^{\circ}_{\text{H}_2/\text{H}^+} = 0\text{ V}$
(Given: $\frac{2.303\text{ RT}}{\text{F}} = 0.059$, $\log 2 = 0.3010$)
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Chemistry: Chemistry NCERT Core] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
$\text{Sol. }\text{H}_2\text{(g)} \longrightarrow 2\text{H}^{\oplus}\text{(aq)} + 2\text{e}^{\ominus}$

$\therefore\text{ E} = \text{E}^{\circ} - \frac{2.303\text{RT}}{\text{nF}}\log \frac{[\text{H}^+]^2}{\text{P}_{\text{H}_2}}$

$[\text{H}^+] = 0.02\text{ M (from HCl)}$

$\text{P}_{\text{H}_2} = 2\text{ atm}$

$\frac{2.303\text{RT}}{\text{F}} = 0.059$

$\text{E} = 0 - \frac{0.059}{2}\log \frac{(0.02)^2}{2}$

$= -0.0295\log\left(\frac{0.0004}{2}\right)$

$\text{E} = -0.0295\log(2 \times 10^{-4})$

$= -0.0295 (\log 2 + \log 10^{-4})$

$= -0.0295 [0.301 - 4] = 0.109\text{ V}$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் D** ($0.109\text{ V}$). பாடம்: Chemistry NCERT Core.
questions.ncert_key_point: [NEET 2026 Official • Numerical / Formula] Official Key: Option D — Chemistry NCERT Core (Class 12).

questions.stem_en: When $1\text{ dm}^3$ of $\text{CO}_2$ gas is passed over hot coke the volume of gaseous mixture after complete reaction at STP becomes $1.4\text{ dm}^3$. The composition of the gaseous mixture at STP is:
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Chemistry: Chemistry NCERT Core] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
$\text{CO}_2 + \text{C(s)} \rightarrow 2\text{CO}$
$$\begin{array}{ccc}
1 & & \\
1-x & & 2x
\end{array}$$
$1 - x + 2x = 1 + x = 1.4$
$x = 0.4\text{ dm}^3$
Volume of $\text{CO}_2 = 1 - 0.4 = 0.6\text{ dm}^3$
Volume of $\text{CO} = 2 \times 0.4 = 0.8\text{ dm}^3$

questions.stem_en:
Given below is an expression for the rate constant of a first-order reaction occurring at a certain temperature, $T$ (K).

$\ln k = 14.34 - \frac{1.25 \times 10^4}{T}$

questions.stem_en: Given below are certain reactions. Identify the reaction for which $\text{K}_\text{p} \neq \text{K}_\text{C}$.
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Chemistry: Chemistry NCERT Core] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
$\text{K}_\text{p} = \text{K}_\text{C}(\text{RT})^{\Delta\text{n}_\text{g}}$

For $\text{K}_\text{p} = \text{K}_\text{C}$ $(\Delta\text{n}_\text{g} = 0)$

$\text{K}_\text{p} \neq \text{K}_\text{C}$ $(\Delta\text{n}_\text{g} \neq 0)$

(1) $\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{g}) + \text{CO}(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons \text{H}_2(\text{g}) + \text{CO}_2(\text{g})$
$\quad\Delta\text{n}_\text{g} = 0$ $(\text{K}_\text{p} = \text{K}_\text{C})$

(2) $\text{N}_2(\text{g}) + 3\text{H}_2(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3(\text{g})$
$\quad\Delta\text{n}_\text{g} = -2$ $(\text{K}_\text{p} \neq \text{K}_\text{C})$

(3) $\text{H}_2(\text{g}) + \text{I}_2(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{HI}(\text{g})$
$\quad\Delta\text{n}_\text{g} = 0$ $(\text{K}_\text{p} = \text{K}_\text{C})$

(4) $\text{N}_2(\text{g}) + \text{O}_2(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NO}(\text{g})$
$\quad\Delta\text{n}_\text{g} = 0$ $(\text{K}_\text{p} = \text{K}_\text{C})$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் B** ($\text{N}_2(\text{g}) + 3\text{H}_2(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3(\text{g})$). பாடம்: Chemistry NCERT Core.

questions.stem_en:
Mixture of chloroform and acetone forms a solution with negative deviation from Raoult's law due to :

(1) Increase in escaping tendency of molecules of each component.
(2) Formation of hydrogen bonding between acetone and chloroform
(3) Stronger intermolecular forces between chloroform molecules than those between chloroform and acetone molecules.
(4) Repulsive forces.

choices.text_en: Increase in escaping tendency of molecules of each component.
choices.text_ta: Increase in escaping tendency of molecules of each component.

choices.text_en: Formation of hydrogen bonding between acetone and chloroform
choices.text_ta: Formation of hydrogen bonding between acetone and chloroform

choices.text_en: Stronger intermolecular forces between chloroform molecules than those between chloroform and acetone molecules.
choices.text_ta: Stronger intermolecular forces between chloroform molecules than those between chloroform and acetone molecules.

questions.explanation_en:
Acetone and chloroform show negative deviation from Raoult's law due to stronger H-bonding between acetone and chloroform mixture.

questions.stem_en:
$2(\text{C}_{51}\text{H}_{98}\text{O}_6) + 145\text{ O}_2 \rightarrow 102\text{ CO}_2 + 98\text{ H}_2\text{O} + \text{energy}$

The Respiratory Quotient (RQ) of a biomolecule used for respiration, as per the above equation would be :
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Botany: Respiration in Plants] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. $\text{R.Q} = \frac{\text{Volume of CO}_2\text{ evolved}}{\text{Volume of O}_2\text{ consumed}}$

As per the given equation,

$2(\text{C}_{51}\text{H}_{98}\text{O}_6) + 145\text{ O}_2 \rightarrow 102\text{ CO}_2 + 98\text{ H}_2\text{O} + \text{Energy}$

Hence the RQ can be calculated as,

$\text{R.Q} = \frac{102}{145} = 0.7$

This value lies between 0.5 and 0.95.

questions.stem_en:
Arrange the following steps of DNA fingerprinting in a correct sequence.

A. Isolation of DNA and its digestion by restriction endonucleases.

B. Hybridisation using a labelled VNTR probe.

C. Transferring of separated DNA fragments to synthetic membranes.

D. Detection of hybridised DNA fragments by autoradiography.

E. Separation of DNA fragments by electrophoresis.

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Botany: Plant Biology & Genetics] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
The following is the correct sequence of steps of DNA fingerprinting.

A. Isolation of DNA and its digestion by restriction endonuclease.

B. Probes made complementary to the VNTR locus are allowed to hybridise with the DNA fragments.

C. The separated DNA fragments are transferred to synthetic membranes made of nylon or nitrocellulose.

D. Finally, the hybridised DNA fragments are detected under X-rays in a technique called autoradiography.

E. DNA fragments are separated based on their size by the technique of gel electrophoresis.

questions.stem_en:
Arrange the following steps of somatic hybridisation in a correct sequence.

A. Digestion of cell walls.
B. Isolation of naked protoplasts.
C. Fusion of protoplasts to get hybrid protoplast.
D. Isolation of single cells from two different varieites of plants.
E. Growing of hybrid protoplast to form a new plant.

questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Zoology: Reproductive Health] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)

Scientist have even isolated single cell protoplasts from two different varieties of plants each having a desirable character and after digesting their cell walls have been able to isolate naked protoplasts (surrounded by plasma membrane) that can be fused to get hybrid protoplast, which can be further grown to form a new plant. questions.stem_en:
Arrange the following events occuring in Renin-Angiotensin mechanism in the correct order:

A. Increase in blood pressure and Glomerular filtration rate
B. Reabsorption of $\text{Na}^+$ and water from distal parts of tubule due to Aldosterone
C. Fall in Glomerular filtration rate
D. Vasoconstriction by Angiotensin II and release of Aldosterone.
E. Renin converts Angiotensinogen into Angiotensin I, followed by Angiotensin II.

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Zoology: Excretory Products and their Elimination] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
**Sol.** The JGA plays a complex regulatory role

* A fall in glomerular blood flow/GFR can activate the JG cells to release renin which converts angiotensinogen in blood to angiotensin I and further to angiotensin II
* Angiotensin II, being a powerful vasoconstrictor, increases the glomerular blood pressure and thereby GFR.
* Angiotensin II activates the adrenal cortex to release aldosterone.
* Aldosterone causes reabsorption of $\text{Na}^+$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ from the distal parts of the tubule. This leads to an increase in blood pressure and GFR.
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் D** (C, E, D, B, A). பாடம்: Excretory Products and their Elimination.

Select the **incorrect** statements from the following:
A. Digestive system in Platyhelminthes is incomplete.
B. Bilateral symmetry is a characteristic feature of adult Echinoderms.
C. Pseudocoelom is possessed by Aschelminthes.
D. Notochord is persistent throughout life in the class Chondrichthyes.
E. Members of class Reptilia maintain a constant body temperature.

questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Zoology: Animal Kingdom] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)

Sol. (A) $\rightarrow$ correct $\rightarrow$ Platyhelminthes have an incomplete digestive system.
(B) $\rightarrow$ incorrect $\rightarrow$ Bilateral symmetry is a characteristic feature of larvae of echinoderms. In adult echinoderms, radial symmetry is seen.
(C) $\rightarrow$ correct $\rightarrow$ Aschelminthes are characterised by the presence of pseudocoelom.
(D) $\rightarrow$ correct $\rightarrow$ Notochord is persistent throughout life in the Chondrichthyes.
(E) $\rightarrow$ incorrect $\rightarrow$ Reptiles are cold-blooded organisms and thus, they cannot maintain a constant body temperature.
Warm-blooded organisms like birds and mammals can maintain a constant body temperature.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Botany — Organisms and Populations (Code 11, Q.156)
questions.stem_en: Which of the following equations depicts Verhulst-Pearl logistic population growth?
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Botany: Organisms and Populations] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. Verhulst-Pearl logistic population growth is depicted by the equation $\frac{\text{dN}}{\text{dt}} = \text{rN}\left(\frac{\text{K} - \text{N}}{\text{K}}\right)$

Where
- $\text{K}$ = Carrying capacity
- $\text{r}$ = Intrinsic rate of natural increase
- $\text{N}$ = Population density at time 't'

questions.stem_en:
Select the **incorrect** statement with reference to Rh grouping.
A. Erythroblastosis foetalis is a condition observed having foetus with $\text{Rh}^{-\text{ve}}$ blood and mother with $\text{Rh}^{+\text{ve}}$ blood.
B. Rh antigen is observed on RBCs in the majority of human beings.
C. Before blood transfusion, Rh group should also be matched.
D. Rh incompatibility is observed when a pregnant mother is $\text{Rh}^{-\text{ve}}$ and the foetus is $\text{Rh}^{+\text{ve}}$.
E. Erythroblastosis foetalis can be avoided by administering anti-Rh antibodies to the mother immediately after the delivery of the second child.

Choose the answer from the options given below :
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Zoology: Animal & Human Biology] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
Sol.
(A) Incorrect $\rightarrow$ A special case of Rh incompatibility has been observed between the $\text{Rh}^{-\text{ve}}$ blood of a pregnant mother with $\text{Rh}^{+\text{ve}}$ blood of the foetus.
(B) Correct $\rightarrow$ Rh antigen is observed on the surface of RBCs of majority (nearly 80 percent) of humans.
(C) Correct $\rightarrow$ Before blood transfusion, Rh group should also be matched to avoid severe problems of destruction of RBCs.
(D) Correct $\rightarrow$ Rh incompatibility (Erythroblastosis foetalis) is observed when a pregnant mother is $\text{Rh}^{-\text{ve}}$ and the foetus is $\text{Rh}^{+\text{ve}}$.
(E) Incorrect $\rightarrow$ Erythroblastosis foetalis can be avoided by administering anti-Rh antibodies to the mother immediately after the delivery of the first child.

Thus, the incorrect statements are (A) and (E).

questions.stem_en:
Choose the correct statements regarding muscle contraction.

A. A motor neuron carries a signal sent by the Central Nervous System (CNS) to the sarcolemma of the muscle fibre.
B. The neural signal generates an action potential which causes the release of $\text{Ca}^{++}$ into sarcoplasm.
C. Increase in $\text{Ca}^{++}$ inactivates the actin for breaking cross bridges.
D. Actin binds to the myosin head to form a cross bridge.
E. Shortening of sarcomere takes place, by pulling actin filaments towards the centre of 'A' band.

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Zoology: Locomotion and Movement] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)

choices.text_en: A, B, D and E only
choices.text_ta: A, B, D and E only

questions.explanation_en:
Sol. Statements A, B, D and E are correct while statement C is incorrect.

A neural signal reaching neuromuscular junction releases a neurotransmitter (Acetylcholine) which generates an action potential in the sarcolemma. This spreads through muscle fibre and causes the release of $\text{Ca}^{++}$ into the sarcoplasm. This $\text{Ca}^{++}$ binds to the subunit of troponin on actin filaments and thereby remove the masking of active site for myosin on actin and hence facilitates the formation of cross bridge.

questions.stem_en:
Which of the following statements are correct with reference to human endoskeleton?

A. Human skull is monocondylic.
B. The joint between any two adjoining vertebrae is a cartilaginous joint.
C. In human beings, the number of cervical vertebrae is seven.
D. All ribs except the last 2 pairs are bicephalic.
E. The occipital bone of skull is articulated with atlas vertebra.

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Zoology: Locomotion and Movement] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. (A) Incorrect : Human skull is dicondylic. The skull region articulates with the superior region of the vertebral column (Atlas) with the help of two occipital condyles.

(B) Correct : The joint present between the adjacent vertebrae of vertebral column is cartilaginous joints.

(C) Correct : There are 7 cervical vertebrae in human beings.

(D) Incorrect : All ribs of humans are bicephalic, *i.e.*, they have two articulation surfaces on their dorsal end.

questions.stem_en:
Spermatogonia undergo a series of cell divisions statements to produce sperms. Select the correct from the following :
A. Spermatogonia always undergo meiotic cell division.
B. Primary spermatocytes divide mitotically to produce secondary spermatocytes.
C. Secondary spermatocytes, through their second meiotic division, produce haploid spermatids.
D. Spermatids produce spermatozoa through mitosis.
E. Spermatids transform into spermatozoa by spermiogenesis.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Botany: Plant Biology & Genetics] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. (A) Incorrect : Spermatogonia undergo mitotic differentiation.
(B) Incorrect : Primary spermatocytes undergo 1$^{st}$ meiotic division to form secondary spermatocytes.
(C) Correct : Secondary spermatocytes undergo 2$^{nd}$ meiotic division to form the haploid spermatids.
(D) Incorrect : Spermatids form spermatozoa through a differentiation process called spermiogenesis.
(E) Correct : Spermatids produce spermatozoa via spermiogenesis.
Thus, the correct statements are (C) and (E) only.

Match List I with List II related to embryonic development at various months of pregnancy:

| | List-I | | List-II |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| A. | The foetus movement starts and hair appears on the head | (I) | 24 weeks of pregnancy |
| B. | The foetus develops limbs and digits | (II) | 20 weeks of pregnancy |
| C. | The foetus develops external genital organs | (III) | 8 weeks of pregnancy |
| D. | The foetus body is covered with fine hair; eyelids separate and eyelashes are formed | (IV) | 12 weeks of pregnancy |

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 Official — Botany: Microbes in Human Welfare] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
Sol.
* By the end of second month of pregnancy (8 weeks), the foetus develops limbs and digits
* By the end of 12 weeks (first trimester) of pregnancy, most of the major organ system are formed. The limbs and external genital organs are also well developed.
* During the fifth month (20 weeks) of pregnancy, the first movements of the foetus and appearance of hair on the head are usually observed.
* By the end of about 24 weeks (ends of second trimester) of pregnancy, the body is covered with fine hair, eye lids separate and eyelashes are formed.

So, the correct match is A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Physics
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Physics — Laws of Motion (Code 50, Q.1)
questions.stem_en: A particle of mass $M$ moves along a horizontal $x$ axis from $x = 0$ to $x = L$. The coefficient of kinetic friction varies as a function of $x$ as $\mu_k(x) = \mu_0 - \alpha x$, where $\mu_0$, $\alpha$ are constants of appropriate dimensions, so that $\mu_k(L) = 0$. The total work done by the frictional force during the motion is $n\mu_0MgL$, where $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity. The value of $n$ is:
questions.stem_ta: [Re-NEET 2026 Official — Physics: Laws of Motion] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
**Sol.** Given $\mu_k(x) = \mu_0 - \alpha x$ and $\mu_k (L) = 0 = \mu_0 - \alpha L \Rightarrow \mu_0 = \alpha L$

Magnitude of work done by frictional force, $W_f = \int dW_f$

where $dW_f = f_k dx = \mu_k N dx = \mu_k Mg dx = (\mu_0 - \alpha x) Mg dx$

$\therefore W_f = \int_{0}^{L} \mu_0 Mg dx - \int_{0}^{L} \alpha Mg x dx = \mu_0 Mg [x]_0^L - \alpha Mg \left[ \frac{x^2}{2} \right]_0^L$

$\Rightarrow n \mu_0 Mg L = \mu_0 Mg L - \left(\frac{\mu_0}{L}\right) Mg \left(\frac{L^2}{2}\right) = \frac{\mu_0 Mg L}{2}$

$\Rightarrow n = \frac{1}{2}$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் D** ($\frac{1}{2}$). பாடம்: Laws of Motion.
questions.ncert_key_point: [Re-NEET 2026 Official • Direct NCERT Concept] Official Key: Option D — Laws of Motion (Class 11).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Physics — Kinetic Theory (Code 50, Q.2)
questions.stem_en: The mean free path of molecules in an ideal gas $A$ is half that of another ideal gas $B$. The diameter of the spherical molecules of gas $A$ is twice the diameter of the molecules of $B$. If number densities of the gases $A$ and $B$ are $n_A$ and $n_B$, respectively, the correct option is:
questions.stem_ta: [Re-NEET 2026 Official — Physics: Kinetic Theory] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
**Sol.** $\lambda_A = \frac{1}{2}\lambda_B$

$\lambda = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2} \pi d^2 n}$

$d_A = 2d_B$

$\lambda_A = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2} \pi d_A^2 n_A}$

$\lambda_B = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2} \pi d_B^2 n_B}$

$\frac{\lambda_A}{\lambda_B} = \frac{1}{2} = \frac{d_B^2}{d_A^2} \frac{n_B}{n_A}$

$\frac{n_A}{n_B} = \frac{2 \cdot d_B^2}{d_A^2}$

$\frac{n_A}{n_B} = \frac{2 \cdot d_B^2}{4 d_B^2} = \frac{1}{2}$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் D** ($n_A = \frac{1}{2}n_B$). பாடம்: Kinetic Theory.

questions.stem_en: For sound waves, if the number of nodes for the $5^{\text{th}}$ harmonic of an open-ended pipe is $n$ and that for the $9^{\text{th}}$ harmonic of the same pipe with one of its ends closed is $m$, the ratio $\frac{n}{m}$ is
questions.stem_ta: [Re-NEET 2026 Official — Physics: Waves] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
**Sol.** For open organ pipe

$\rightarrow$ Number of nodes are same as number of harmonics

$\therefore n = 5$

For closed organ pipe

$\rightarrow$ There are only odd harmonics

For $1^{\text{st}}$ harmonic $\rightarrow$ Number of node $\rightarrow 1$

For $3^{\text{rd}}$ harmonic $\rightarrow$ Number of node $\rightarrow 2$

For $5^{\text{th}}$ harmonic $\rightarrow$ Number of node $\rightarrow 3$

For $7^{\text{th}}$ harmonic $\rightarrow$ Number of node $\rightarrow 4$

For $9^{\text{th}}$ harmonic $\rightarrow$ Number of node $\rightarrow 5$

$\therefore m = 5$

$\rightarrow \frac{n}{m} = \frac{5}{5} = 1$

questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Physics — Moving Charges and Magnetism (Code 50, Q.5)
questions.stem_en: Consider a long solenoid of length $l$ and radius $r$. If $n$ is the number of turns per unit length and $\mu_0$ is the permeability of free space, the inductance of the solenoid is :
questions.stem_ta: [Re-NEET 2026 Official — Physics: Moving Charges and Magnetism] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
**Sol.** Self inductance of solenoid

$L = \frac{N\phi}{i}$

$L = \frac{NBA}{i}$

$L = \frac{N\mu_0 niA}{i}\ \left[n = \frac{N}{l}\right]$

$L = N\mu_0 nA$

$L = \left(\frac{N}{l}\right)\mu_0 nAl$

$L = \mu_0 n^2 Al$

$L = \mu_0 n^2 \pi r^2 l\ \left[\because A = \pi r^2\right]$

questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Physics — Nuclei (Code 50, Q.7)
questions.stem_en:
Consider the following nuclear reaction
${}^{238}\text{U} \longrightarrow {}^{234}\text{Th} + {}^4\text{He}$
Take masses of ${}^{238}\text{U}$, ${}^{234}\text{Th}$ and ${}^4\text{He}$ as $238.050\text{ u}$, $234.043\text{ u}$ and $4.003\text{ u}$, respectively. The $Q$ value for the reaction, in keV, is:
[Given: $1\text{ u} = 931.5\text{ MeV c}^{-2}$]
questions.stem_ta: [Re-NEET 2026 Official — Physics: Nuclei] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. Q-value for the nuclear reaction is given by, $Q = \Delta m c^2$
$${}^{238}\text{U} \longrightarrow {}^{234}\text{Th} + {}^4\text{He}\text{ has mass defect }\Delta m = m_{\text{reactants}} - m_{\text{products}}$$
$\Rightarrow \Delta m = 238.050 - (234.043 + 4.003) = 0.004\text{ u}$
$\therefore Q = 0.004 \times 931.5\text{ MeV} = 3.726\text{ MeV} = 3726\text{ keV}$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் A** (3726). பாடம்: Nuclei.

The minimum magnitude of $h$ so that the wire $A$ does not rise from the floor is:

$[g\text{ is the acceleration due to gravity and }\mu_0\text{ is the permeability of free space.}]$

questions.stem_en:
In an adiabatic expansion, the temperature of one mole of an ideal monatomic gas ($\gamma = 5/3$) decreases from $60\text{ K}$ to $50\text{ K}$. The work done by the gas in the process is:
(Take the universal gas constant as $R = 8.3\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}$)
questions.stem_ta: [Re-NEET 2026 Official — Physics: Work, Energy and Power] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. Work done in adiabatic process

$W = \frac{nR\Delta T}{1-\gamma}$

$\Delta T = -10\text{K}$

$W = \frac{1 \times 8.3 \times (-10)}{1 - \frac{5}{3}}$

$W = \frac{83 \times 3}{2}$

$W = 124.5\text{ J}$

questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Physics — Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter (Code 50, Q.18)
questions.stem_en: A ray of light with wavelength $\lambda$ is incident on three different photoelectric cells namely 1, 2 and 3. The threshold wavelength of these photoelectric cells are $\lambda_1, \lambda_2,$ and $\lambda_3,$ respectively and the magnitude of stopping potentials of these cells are $V_1, V_2$ and $V_3$, respectively. The relation between $\lambda$ and threshold wavelengths are $\lambda_1 \lambda$ and $\lambda_3 \gg \lambda$. The correct option is:
questions.stem_ta: [Re-NEET 2026 Official — Physics: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. For ejection of electron energy of incident photon should be greater than work function
$\phi = \frac{hc}{\lambda}$
$\phi_1 = \frac{hc}{\lambda_1}$
$\lambda_1 \phi$
No electron will eject
$V_1 = 0$
By Einstein photoelectric equation
$\phi = \phi_0 + eV$
$\lambda_2 > \lambda$
$\lambda_3 \gg \lambda$
$\phi > \phi_2$
$\phi \gg \phi_3$
So, $V_3 > V_2$

questions.stem_en:
A photon and an electron, each of $20\text{ eV}$ energy, move in free space. The ratio of linear momentum of electron $p_e$ to that of photon $p_{Ph}$, $\frac{p_e}{p_{Ph}}$ is:

[Take speed of light $= 3 \times 10^8\text{ ms}^{-1}$, charge of electron $= -1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$ and mass of electron $= 9 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}$]
questions.stem_ta: [Re-NEET 2026 Official — Physics: Laws of Motion] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. $E_e = E_{Ph} = 20\text{ eV}$

$\Rightarrow P_e = \sqrt{2m_e E_e}, P_{Ph} = \frac{E_{Ph}}{c}$

$$\Rightarrow \frac{P_e}{P_{Ph}} = \frac{\sqrt{2m_e E_e}}{E_{Ph}} c = \sqrt{\frac{2m_e}{E_{Ph}}} c$$

$$\frac{P_e}{P_{Ph}} = \sqrt{\frac{2 \times 9 \times 10^{-31}}{20 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}}} \times 3 \times 10^8$$

$= \frac{3}{4} \times 10^{-6} \times 3 \times 10^8 = \frac{900}{4} = 225$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் C** (225). பாடம்: Laws of Motion.

questions.stem_en: The temperature of a metallic sphere of radius $R$ is increased by a small amount $\Delta T$. If the linear coefficient of thermal expansion of the metal is $\alpha$, the approximate increase in the volume of the sphere is:
questions.stem_ta: [Re-NEET 2026 Official — Physics: Physics NCERT Core] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)

Volume of the sphere, $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi R^3$

Velocity $v$ as a function of $n$ is given by

$v^2 = \omega^2\left(A^2 - x^2\right)$

$\frac{v^2}{\omega^2} + x^2 = A^2$

Given that above equation is of a circle

Hence, $\omega^2 = 1$

$\frac{k}{m} = 1$

$k = m$

An ac voltage $V = 220\sin(2 \times 10^3 t)\text{ Volt}$ is applied to a series LCR circuit. Then the current amplitude in this circuit is:

(Given : $L = 10\text{ mH}$, $C = 25\ \mu\text{F}$, $R = 100\ \Omega$)

questions.explanation_en:
Sol. Angular frequency of $AC$ source, $\omega = 2 \times 10^3\text{ rad/s}$

Inductive reactance, $X_L = \omega L = (2\times 10^3) \times (10\times 10^{-3}) = 20\ \Omega$

Capacitive reactance, $X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} = \frac{1}{(2\times 10^3)\times(25\times 10^{-6})} = 20\ \Omega$

Impedance $Z$ for circuit $= R$ ($\dots X_L = X_C$ and circuit is at resonance)

$\therefore$ current amplitude, $i_0 = \frac{V_0}{Z} = \frac{V_0}{R} = \frac{220}{100} = 2.2\text{ A}$

questions.stem_en: An ideal gas is made of polyatomic molecules. Each of the molecules has three translational, three rotational and $f$ number of vibrational modes. If the ratio of heat capacities $C_P/C_V$ of the gas is $8/7$, then the value of $f$ is:

questions.explanation_en:
The total internal energy for one mole of gas, $U$
$= \left(\frac{3}{2}k_BT + \frac{3}{2}k_BT + fk_BT\right) N_A$
$= (3 + f)k_B T N_A = (3+f)RT$
$\therefore \quad C_V = \frac{dU}{dT} = (3 + f)R$
$C_P = C_V + R = (4 + f)R$
$\Rightarrow \quad \frac{C_P}{C_V} = \frac{4 + f}{3 + f} = \frac{8}{7} \text{ (given)}$
$\Rightarrow f = 4$

For a salt **XY**, which is a strong electrolyte, the plot of $\Lambda_{\text{m}}$ versus $\sqrt{\text{c}}$ has a slope of $-90.0\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-3/2}\text{ L}^{1/2}$ at $298\text{ K}$. At $0.01\text{ M}$ concentration of **XY**, the value of $\Lambda_{\text{m}}$ is $145.0\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$. The limiting molar conductivity of $\text{Y}^-$ ion ($\lambda_{\text{Y}^-}^0$, in $\text{S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$) at $298\text{ K}$ will be

questions.stem_ta: [Re-NEET 2026 Official — Chemistry: Electrochemistry] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)

**Sol.** $\text{y} = \text{mx} + \text{c}$

$\text{slope} = -90$

questions.stem_en:
Given below are two statements :

**Statement-I :** Heating $\text{NaCl}$ with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ and $\text{MnO}_2$ results in oxidation of $\text{Mn}$.

**Statement-II :** Heating $\text{NaI}$ with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ and $\text{MnO}_2$ results in reduction of $\text{Mn}$.

In light of the above statements, choose the **most appropriate** answer from the options given below.
questions.stem_ta: [Re-NEET 2026 Official — Chemistry: Chemistry NCERT Core] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. Statement-I : (False)

$$2\text{NaCl} + \overset{+4}{\text{MnO}}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4 + \overset{+2}{\text{MnSO}}_4 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{Cl}_2$$

So, reduction of Mn is taking place.

Statement-II : (True)

$$2\text{NaI} + \overset{+4}{\text{MnO}}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4 + \overset{+2}{\text{MnSO}}_4 + \text{I}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

So, Mn has undergone reduction.

questions.stem_en: Length of the stem at time 0 is 20 cm. The arithmetic growth rate is 30 cm per day. What is the length of the stem at the end of the $7^{\text{th}}$ day?
questions.stem_ta: [Re-NEET 2026 Official — Botany: Plant Biology & Genetics] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. Arithmetic growth can be expressed as :

$L_t = L_0 + rt$ [where, $L_t$ = length at time 't', $L_0$ = Length at time 'zero', $r$ = growth rate]

$L_{\text{7th day}} \Rightarrow 20 + 30 \times 7$

$\Rightarrow 20 + 210$

$\Rightarrow 230\text{ cm}$

The length of the stem at the end of $7^{\text{th}}$ day is 230 cm.
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் C** (230 cm). பாடம்: Plant Biology & Genetics.

questions.stem_ta: [Re-NEET 2026 Official — Botany: Plant Biology & Genetics] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
The per-capita birth rate of bacteria is 0.002.

The per-capita death rate of bacteria is 0.002.

The population dynamic equation is
$\frac{dN}{dt} = (b - d)N$

Since $r = (b - d) = 0.002 - 0.002 = 0$
$\frac{dN}{dt} = 0$

So, the population remains constant at all times. Thus, even after 10 generations, the expected number of cells will be 10 million.

questions.stem_en:
Which of the following statements are **Correct** ?

(a) Energy flow from producers to consumers is unidirectional

(b) Energy pyramid can never be inverted

(c) Transfer of energy follows the $1\%$ law

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :

questions.explanation_en:
Energy flow is unidirectional. First plants capture solar energy and then, food is transferred from the producers to decomposers.

Pyramid of energy is always upright. It can never be inverted, because when energy flows from a particular trophic level to the next trophic level, some energy is always lost as heat at each step.

The transfer of energy follows 10 per cent law – only 10 per cent of the energy is transferred to each trophic level from the lower trophic level.

$FS = \Delta K\cdot E$

$\Rightarrow -FS = k_f - k_i$

Magnetic force $= \frac{mv^2}{r}$

$evB = \frac{mv^2}{r}$

$v = \frac{eBr}{m}$

$\phi = BA$

$\frac{nh}{e} = B\pi r^2$

$\mu = IA$

$\mu = \frac{neh}{2\pi m}$

for $n = 1$

$\mu = \frac{eh}{2\pi m}$

questions.stem_en: Two cities $X$ and $Y$ are connected by a regular bus service with a bus leaving in either direction every $T$ min. A girl is driving scooty with a speed of $60\text{ km/h}$ in the direction $X$ to $Y$ notices that a bus goes past her every $30$ minutes in the direction of her motion, and every $10$ minutes in the opposite direction. questions.explanation_en:
$X \to Y$

Let velocity of bus $= v\text{ km/hr}$

Relative velocity of bus w.r.t. scooty $= (v - 60)$

Distance between 2 consecutive buses $= vT$

$(v - 60)30 = vT$ ...(i)

$Y \to X$

$(v + 60)10 = vT$ ...(ii)

Equating (1) and (2)

$(v - 60)30 = (v + 60)10$

$\therefore v = 120\text{ km/hr}$

$T = 15\text{ min}$

A balloon is made of a material of surface tension $S$ and its inflation outlet (from where gas is filled in it) has small area $A$. It is filled with a gas of density $
ho$and takes a spherical shape of radius$R$. When the gas is allowed to flow freely out of it, its radius$r$changes from$R$to 0 (zero) in time$T$. If the speed$v(r)$of gas coming out of the balloon depends on$r$as$r^a$and$T \propto S^{\alpha} A^{\beta} \rho^{\gamma} R^{\delta}$ then
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2025 Official — Physics: Mechanical Properties of Fluids] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. $T \propto S^{\alpha} A^{\beta} \rho^{\gamma} R^{\delta}$

$\mathrm{M}^0\mathrm{L}^0\mathrm{T}^1 = K(\mathrm{MT}^{-2})^{\alpha} (\mathrm{L}^2)^{\beta} (\mathrm{ML}^{-3})^{\gamma} \mathrm{L}^{\delta}$

$\mathrm{M}^0\mathrm{L}^0\mathrm{T}^1 = K[\mathrm{M}^{\alpha + \gamma} \mathrm{L}^{2\beta - 3\gamma + \delta} \mathrm{T}^{-2\alpha}]$

$-2\alpha = 1 \implies \alpha = -\frac{1}{2}$

$\alpha + \gamma = 0 \implies \gamma = \frac{1}{2}$

$2\beta - 3\gamma + \delta = 0$

$2\beta - 3\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) + \delta = 0$

By hit and trial (using option (1))

Put $\beta = -1$

$2(-1) - \frac{3}{2} + \delta = 0 \quad \therefore \delta = \frac{7}{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Physics — Gravitation (Code 45, Q.31)
questions.stem_en: The radius of Martian orbit around the Sun is about 4 times the radius of the orbit of Mercury. The Martian year is 687 Earth days. Then which of the following is the length of 1 year on Mercury?
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2025 Official — Physics: Gravitation] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. Applying Kepler's $3^{\text{rd}}$ law : $T^2 \propto R^3$
Radius of Martian orbit, $R' = 4R$
$\left(\frac{T'}{T}\right)^2 = \left(\frac{R'}{R}\right)^3 = \left(\frac{4R}{R}\right)^3 = 4^3 = 64 \Rightarrow \frac{T'}{T} = 8$
$\therefore$ Length of 1 year on Mercury = $T = \frac{T'}{8} = \frac{687}{8} = 85.88$ days
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் A** (88 earth days). பாடம்: Gravitation.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Physics — Physics NCERT Core (Code 45, Q.32)
questions.stem_en: A body weighs 48 N on the surface of the earth. The gravitational force experienced by the body due to the earth at a height equal to one-third the radius of the earth from its surface is :
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2025 Official — Physics: Physics NCERT Core] (ஆங்கில மூல வினா மேலே / கீழே உள்ளது)
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. $W = mg$ and $g = \frac{GM}{R^2}$, $g_h = \frac{GM}{(R+h)^2}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{W_h}{W} = \frac{m g_h}{m g} = \frac{g_h}{g} = \frac{R^2}{(R+h)^2}$ $\left(h = \frac{R}{3}\right)$
$\Rightarrow \frac{W_h}{W} = \frac{R^2}{\left(R + \frac{R}{3}\right)^2} = \frac{R^2}{\left(\frac{4R}{3}\right)^2} = \frac{9}{16}$
$\Rightarrow W_h = \frac{9}{16}W = \frac{9}{16} \times 48\quad [W = 48\text{ N}]$
$= 27\text{ N}$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் B** (27 N). பாடம்: Physics NCERT Core.
